# Citing this book {#sec-citing .unnumbered}

This is a living online book. The website is the canonical reading edition and may change as errors are corrected and further subject-matter validation is completed. Numbered releases will provide immutable snapshots for citations that need to identify an exact version.

## Current citation

Until the first archived release receives a DOI, cite the online book as:

> Delius, Gustav, ed. (2026). *Affine Toda field theory: A graduate introduction, leading into current research*. Living online monograph. <https://gustavdelius.github.io/affine_toda/>.

The coordinating editor and the limited role of the subject-matter validators are described in @sec-about. Validators are not authors or editors of the whole book, and their names are not included in the book-level citation.

### BibTeX

```bibtex
@book{delius_affine_toda_2026,
  editor = {Delius, Gustav},
  title  = {Affine Toda Field Theory: A Graduate Introduction, Leading into Current Research},
  year   = {2026},
  url    = {https://gustavdelius.github.io/affine_toda/},
  note   = {Living online monograph; AI-drafted, with validation scoped to cited researchers' own work}
}
```

### RIS

```text
TY  - BOOK
TI  - Affine Toda field theory: A graduate introduction, leading into current research
ED  - Delius, Gustav
PY  - 2026
UR  - https://gustavdelius.github.io/affine_toda/
N1  - Living online monograph; AI-drafted, with validation scoped to cited researchers' own work
ER  -
```

## DOI and versions

The DOI is pending the first versioned archival release. Once Zenodo has reserved it, this page and the book metadata will give two identifiers:

- the **concept DOI**, for citing the evolving book as a whole; and
- a **version DOI**, for citing the exact release used.

For claims depending on an equation, proof, computation or validation status, cite a version DOI and give the chapter, section or equation identifier. For a general reference to the project, use the concept DOI.

The supporting software is distributed under the MIT License, while the book text and figures are distributed under CC BY 4.0. Licensing governs reuse; it does not change the preferred scholarly citation above.
